body: Micro-dramas are short shows made for phones, with each episode lasting only one or two minutes.
微短剧是专为手机制作的短剧，每集只有一两分钟。
They are cheap to make, fast to watch, and full of cliffhangers that keep viewers tapping for the next episode.
它们制作成本低、观看速度快，而且充满悬念，让观众忍不住点开下一集。
Some people worry they shorten our attention span, while others see them as a new form of storytelling for busy lives.
有人担心它们让注意力越来越短，也有人认为这是忙碌生活里的新型讲故事方式。

articles.en: How do we adapt to the cold?
body: Some people shiver at the first autumn wind, while others swim in icy water and call it fun.
有人秋风一吹就发抖，有人却在冰水里游泳还乐在其中。
Scientists say our bodies can slowly get used to low temperatures through a process called acclimatisation.
科学家说，人体可以通过「环境适应」这个过程慢慢习惯低温。
Regular, gentle exposure to the cold may even train the body to burn energy better and feel less discomfort.
规律而温和地接触寒冷，甚至能训练身体更好地消耗能量，减少不适感。

articles.en: Why are some animals black and white?
articles.zh: 为什么有些动物是黑白配色？
body: Zebras, pandas and penguins all wear black and white, but for very different reasons.
斑马、熊猫和企鹅都穿着黑白「外套」，但原因大不相同。
A zebra's stripes may confuse biting insects, making it harder for them to land on the skin.
斑马的条纹可能会迷惑叮咬的昆虫，让它们更难落在皮肤上。
For pandas, the bold pattern could help them hide in snow and shadow, or send signals to each other.
对熊猫来说，醒目的黑白图案可能帮它们隐藏在雪地和阴影中，或者用来互相传递信号。

articles.zh: 重新认识阅读障碍：隐藏的超能力？
body: Dyslexia makes reading and spelling harder, and many children with it feel left behind at school.
阅读障碍会让读写变得困难，许多有阅读障碍的孩子在学校感觉被落下了。
But researchers now believe dyslexic brains are often stronger at big-picture thinking, creativity and problem-solving.
但研究者现在认为，有阅读障碍的大脑往往更擅长全局思考、创造力和解决问题。
Instead of calling it a weakness, some experts prefer to see it as a different — and valuable — way of thinking.
有些专家不再把它称为缺陷，而是把它看作一种不同且珍贵的思维方式。
Many of us refuse certain foods as children, then wake up one day and find we actually enjoy them.
很多人小时候拒绝某些食物，某天却突然发现自己居然爱上了它们。
Taste is not fixed: repeated small tries can slowly teach the brain to accept bitter or strange flavours.
口味不是一成不变的：反复少量尝试，可以慢慢让大脑接受苦味或奇怪的味道。
Food scientists suggest pairing a disliked food with something you love, so good feelings rub off on it.
食品科学家建议把讨厌的食物和喜欢的食物搭配着吃，让好感「传染」过去。
tips: 慢慢培养出的爱好（口味）
